title: Umbraflow RuntimeModel v2
description: Field shapes for the trusted RuntimeModel parser and its two-stage results. Cross-reference, coverage, placement and same-cycle authority rules are enforced by the trusted Luau compiler/resolver.

layout.$comment: How much of the Binding's rectangle this Reader is asserting about. single_line says the rectangle holds exactly one line and skips line detection entirely, which is cheaper and immune to a detector that splits one label in two. block says the count is not known, so every line the detector finds inside that rectangle is located and read. There is no default and nothing is inferred: under single_line a rectangle that in fact holds several lines reads as one run of nonsense rather than failing, so which of the two this Reader is has to be stated by whoever drew the rectangle.

surface_identity.$comment: A Surface is present only when every listed Binding is present. Alternative visual states belong to one Binding's variants rather than creating a disjunction here.

detected_collection_placement.$comment: A search region plus the trusted block Reader that detects every item inside it. search_rect bounds the measurement and is never evidence by itself. Each detected line supplies one item's exact image-space rectangle. order turns those measured rectangles into stable zero-based indices; overlapping spans on that axis are ambiguous and the resolver refuses them instead of inheriting detector enumeration order. slots describes the regular centred layout on that same axis. Its origin is the measured item-origin coordinate for a one-item layout. For n items, slot k is origin - (n - 1) * pitch / 2 + k * pitch. pitch must be even so every centred layout lands on integer coordinates.

slots.$comment: origin is the one-item slot coordinate on order's axis. pitch is the positive distance between adjacent slots and is even because halving an odd pitch would put centred even-cardinality layouts between integer pixels. tolerance is the maximum distance between a measured item origin and its assigned slot.

collection.$comment: An ordered, variable-cardinality collection on one Surface. Its item count and item placements are runtime results, never authored geometry. The placement's Reader is detector evidence for the items and must declare block layout. A Reader named in reads REPORTS from each measured item rectangle and never decides whether the Collection or an item exists; only the placement's detector Reader decides that. predicate conditionally enumerates members using one of those declared per-item Readers; changing it changes the returned count and ordered member list, never the detector's spatial identity. A click action's offset is the [dx, dy] delta from ONE selected item's measured origin. The item is chosen by its zero-based index, and the derived point must remain inside the frame; leaving it is a refusal rather than a clamp. This is the same origin-delta rule collection_read.offset uses because a Collection has no single fixed placement in which an action_point could live.

collection_read_offset.$comment: The [dx, dy] delta applied to one measured item's origin. Either component may be negative.

collection_read.$comment: One reporting-only Reader, an origin delta, and an absolute size; the resulting rectangle must remain wholly inside the frame, and leaving it is a refusal rather than a clamp. An item is one line of text whose width belongs to that text, while a read placed against it belongs to the containing element and therefore has that element's fixed extent.

key_action.$comment: One keystroke the target's own UI prints as an affordance. It carries no coordinate: which key is pressed is the whole of what is delivered, and the Binding's placement exists here to hold the proof_locator's rectangle rather than to aim anything. proof_locator means what it means for a click -- not proof the keystroke happened, but that a template belonging to this Binding's own detector was re-measured present on this very cycle, so the screen that accepts the key is the screen that is showing.

key.$comment: The key spelled exactly as the target prints it. The accepted vocabulary is closed and is defined once, in the trusted C++ KeyName, which refuses a name outside it and prints the whole set it refused against; restating that set here would be a second spelling of one rule. This names a key on the TARGET's keyboard and never one the operator presses.

drag_action.$comment: One atomic drag beginning at fixed_placement.action_point and ending at that point plus offset. duration_ms is project-owned measured behavior with no default. The target may move while the gesture runs; the delivery layer keeps target identity fenced, completes the declared path, ends at rest, and releases before returning.

variants.$comment: The visual states sharing this Binding's target, placement, actions and reads. Exactly one detector must be satisfied for the Binding to be present; two satisfied variants are an ambiguity, never a declaration-order pick. Variant names are unique within the Binding and the trusted compiler enforces that relation.

reads.$comment: Readers whose normalised value this Binding reports once it is measured present. A reader named here never decides the detector: text is evidence about what is on a Surface, never the identity of one. Absent is the empty list, which is what most Bindings declare; making it required would say nothing on every Binding that reports nothing.

allOf.$comment: A Binding click aims through fixed_placement.action_point and carries no offset; a Binding drag declares its endpoint as an offset from that same measured point.

action_point exists exactly when some action needs a coordinate. The condition reads 'every action names no coordinate', which is also true of a Binding granting no action at all, so both of those forbid the point and a click or drag requires one.

transition_trigger.$comment: The action that declares policy intent. Exactly one owner is named: a Binding, or a Collection whose item will be chosen by index when the action is resolved. An observed transition names its declared transition by ID and never duplicates this trigger, so replay data cannot become a second policy authority.

transition.$comment: One declared policy transition stored in RuntimeModel.transitions. Its destination is immutable model input; observed destinations use observed_transition instead of changing this record.

observed_transition.$comment: One replayable observation stored outside RuntimeModel. transition joins it to declared policy; observed_to_surfaces records what resolution actually reached and never replaces the declaration's to_surfaces.

transition_comparison.$comment: The offline comparison of one observed_transition with its declared policy. Both destinations are reported so a mismatch remains reviewable without consulting mutable model state.

connectivity_colour_key.$comment: The project owns the colour key because line colour is target-specific authored knowledge, while the model only evaluates samples against it. No separate runtime gate is needed for that ownership ruling: the closed RuntimeModel schema admits the key only inside the project's stitched_map declaration.

stitched_map.$comment: A connectivity evaluation over one assembled map, never one screenful. The named Collection supplies the conditionally enumerated nodes; every unordered node pair is read against the project-owned colour key, and minimum_ratio decides its edge.

unknown_reason.$comment: Why one measurement could not be decided. One closed vocabulary, referenced by everything that reports an Unknown, because a reason spelled twice is two vocabularies that agree by test rather than by construction. Nothing-was-measured is not one reason, because a consumer that fails closed acts differently on each: not_measured is that nobody asked, budget_exhausted is that the Host stopped looking inside a ceiling the caller can raise or spend over a fresh cycle, stale_cycle is that the frame it would have measured had expired, and host_unavailable is that it could not look at all. None of them is locator_failed, which claims something looked and did not find.

reading_line.$comment: One line of one reading: the normalised text, and the rectangle the frame held that text in. Under a block Reader the rectangle is the detector's own measurement and is in the coordinate space of the IMAGE rather than of the Reader's rectangle; under a single_line Reader nothing was located, so it is the Binding's declared placement rect and cannot move between two captures at all.

binding_reading.$comment: One reading the resolver reports for a Binding it measured present, under a Reader that Binding named in reads. Three outcomes and no fourth: read carries the lines, absent says the Reader found no text in that rectangle, unknown says it could not decide and carries why. The two failures are reported rather than dropped because a consumer that cannot tell 'nothing is written here' from 'this frame was unreadable' has to fail closed on one blurry capture. A reading is a LIST of lines whatever the Reader's layout: a single_line Reader reports one element, not a second shape, because one fact spelled two ways makes every consumer ask which spelling it was handed. What is still not carried is the score: it has already been compared against the Reader's confidence_floor, and it differs between two captures of one unchanged screen while this value is hashed into a decision basis. A bounded reason is safe there; a float is not. Each line's RECT is carried and IS hashed with the rest of this document, and that is a ruling rather than an oversight: the score has no decision left to take once the floor has judged it, while the rect is where a consumer acts, so a basis that omitted it would let a frozen plan be re-derived into a different action without the basis moving. Unsoundness outranks an extra approval. There is still no pre-normalisation text, because that is the raw read the Reader exists to narrow.

state_readings.$comment: Every reading a resolved state reports, ordered by ui_target then reader so one world produces one document. One entry per Reader every reporting Binding named, whatever the outcome, so the length is decided by the model and the resolved stack rather than by what the Host managed to answer. A Binding owns the visual variants that share its placement and reads, so changing which one matches does not change the reporting subject. Multiple present Bindings sharing a UiTarget still report nothing for it because they are distinct placements or roles and therefore remain ambiguous.

collection_item.$comment: One item located by a collection's trusted block Reader. index is the zero-based slot ordinal declared by the collection, not the Reader adapter's enumeration order; a partial collection can therefore have gaps between indices. rect is copied exactly from the detected line in image coordinates.

readings.$comment: One result for every reporting-only Reader the Collection declares, in declaration order.

resolved_collection.$comment: The result of resolving one declared collection against one resolved state in the same live cycle. count is the number of detected items. complete and partial carry those measured items; partial slot indices may contain gaps. unknown means no detected-item-to-layout assignment exists within the search rectangle and carries no items list. An absent Reader result is a complete collection with count zero. Unknown Reader evidence or ambiguous spatial order still produces no resolved_collection.

unknown_state.$comment: diagnostic is optional because only visible content that matches no Surface emits T-004 detail; other unknown states already carry their reason.

key.$comment: The key the authorized action names, copied from the Binding action so the Host is told what to deliver without reading the model. Same closed vocabulary as key_action.key, and same single definition.
